questions.question_text: You are approaching a crossroads where the priority situation is not clear to you straightaway. What do you do?

options.a: Wait, observe and come to an agreement with others, if necessary.
options.b: Proceed at your current speed assuming the other drivers will yield.
options.c: Assert your right-of-way if you are travelling on the wider and better-developed road.

questions.explanation: When you arrive at an intersection where the right-of-way is unclear or confusing, you must not assume other drivers will yield to you. Instead, the rule dictates that you are required to hold back, carefully observe the actions of other road users, and communicate with them (such as through hand signals) to reach a mutual agreement before proceeding safely.

questions.question_text: At a junction, a police officer is controlling traffic. Their arm is raised straight up. What does this signal mean?

options.a: Cross the crossroads at a brisk pace to clear the intersection.
options.b: The right-of-way rule 'right before left' immediately applies.
options.c: Wait at the crossroads as it is a signal to stop.

questions.explanation: When a police officer directing traffic raises their arm straight up, it acts exactly like an amber traffic light. This signal dictates that all vehicles currently approaching the intersection must wait and prepare to stop, as the officer is about to change the direction of flowing traffic.

questions.question_text: You want to turn left from this farm track. Referring to the image, who must wait?

options.a: Traffic on the main road must give way to you.
options.b: The car coming from the farm track must wait.
options.c: The driver with the heavier vehicle is granted right of way.

questions.explanation: In this scenario, the car emerging from the farm track is joining a public road from a non-public road or private driveway. The rule dictates that any vehicle leaving a farm track must give way to all cross traffic already established on the public road, meaning the car on the track must wait for you to pass.

questions.question_text: What is the correct procedure at a 4-way-stop?

options.a: The stopped vehicle which arrived first shall have priority to move off first.
options.b: The vehicle turning left always has priority, regardless of arrival order.
options.c: All drivers must give way to traffic approaching from their right.

questions.explanation: At an intersection controlled by four STOP signs, priority is not determined by who is turning or who is on the right. Instead, the rule dictates a first-come, first-served approach, meaning the specific vehicle that arrives and comes to a complete halt at their stop line first is granted the priority to move off first.

questions.question_text: Referring to the image, you are driving towards a traffic light that is flashing amber. What is the correct procedure?

options.a: Both vehicles must wait till the traffic light changes to yellow.
options.b: The green vehicle ahead may proceed.
options.c: I may turn without waiting by observing the traffic sign.

questions.explanation: A flashing amber light indicates that the traffic light system is currently out of service or in caution mode, so it no longer dictates priority. Because of this, you must obey the permanent priority signs present at the intersection, which in this case means you can proceed by observing the signs rather than waiting for the light to change.

questions.question_text: In which cases are you not allowed to drive into the crossroads even though the traffic light is 'green'?

options.a: If the vehicle behind you is driving too close and tailgating.
options.b: If you would have to wait on the crossroads because of traffic congestion.
options.c: If you are turning right and there are no pedestrians waiting.

questions.explanation: Even when your traffic light is green, the rule strictly forbids you from driving into the crossroads if the traffic ahead of you is backed up. Entering the intersection under these conditions would cause your vehicle to physically block cross traffic once their light turns green, leading to complete gridlock.

questions.question_text: Referring to the image, which conduct is correct?

options.a: I may proceed immediately because I am going straight.
options.b: I have priority over the yellow car, but must wait for the red car.
options.c: The red and yellow car proceed first.

questions.explanation: Because this intersection lacks any priority signs, the basic 'right before left' rule applies, meaning every driver must give way to the vehicle approaching from their immediate right. The red car has no one on its right, so it goes first, followed by the yellow car, which means you must wait until both have cleared the junction.

questions.question_text: At which places where there are no traffic signs regulating priority does the rule 'right before left' apply?

options.b: Only at roundabouts and traffic-calmed areas.
options.c: Only on roads located outside built-up residential areas.

questions.explanation: The 'right before left' rule is the universal default standard for determining priority when there are no traffic lights, police officers, or priority signs present. Therefore, this rule automatically applies at any standard crossroads or junction where roads of equal importance meet without specific regulatory signage.

questions.question_text: In the image, you are stopped at the line. Which conduct is correct?

options.a: I am permitted to proceed before the bus if I accelerate quickly.
options.b: I must first stop at the stop line, then allow both the cyclist and bus to pass.
options.c: I must allow the bus to proceed but have priority over the cyclist.

questions.explanation: The STOP sign on your road mandates that you must come to a complete halt at the stop line, regardless of whether the junction looks clear. Furthermore, because you are at a stop sign, the intersecting road is the priority road, so you must allow all cross traffic, including both the bus and the cyclist, to safely pass before you can proceed.

questions.question_text: A police officer is regulating the traffic at a crossroads where there are also traffic signs governing priority. What applies?

options.c: The general rule of 'right before left'.

questions.explanation: The hierarchy of road rules states that commands given by a live police officer take absolute precedence over all static traffic signs or automated traffic lights. Therefore, if an officer is actively regulating the intersection, you must follow their hand signals and entirely ignore the priority signs.

questions.question_text: Referring to the traffic lights in the image, what is permitted?

options.a: You must wait for the main light to turn green before turning right.
options.b: You may only turn right after coming to a complete stop and sounding your horn.
options.c: You may turn right from the right lane when there is no obstruction or danger to others.

questions.explanation: The presence of a secondary green arrow light pointing right means you are explicitly authorized to make a right turn even if the main circular traffic light is red. This signal dictates that as long as you are in the correct right-turning lane, you may proceed without stopping, provided you do not obstruct or endanger others.

questions.question_text: In the image, you intend to turn right. The cyclist is proceeding straight. Which conduct is correct?

options.a: The motorcyclist must wait for me.
options.b: I must allow the cyclist to pass.
options.c: We have equal priority so we must come to an agreement.

questions.explanation: When you are preparing to turn right, the rule requires you to yield to any oncoming traffic that is traveling straight through the intersection. Because the cyclist is moving straight ahead and your intended turn would cut directly across their path, you must wait and allow the cyclist to pass first.

questions.question_text: You want to cross a priority road. The sight to both sides is greatly impaired by parked vehicles. What do you do?

options.a: Drive onto the crossroads slowly and carefully.
options.b: Sound your horn to warn unseen traffic before proceeding quickly.
options.c: Wait until another vehicle goes and follow them closely to be safe.

questions.explanation: When your line of sight at an intersection is blocked by parked vehicles, you cannot safely determine if the priority road is clear. The rule for this situation dictates that you must edge your vehicle forward very slowly and carefully until you gain a clear view of the cross traffic, rather than blindly driving out or relying solely on your horn.

questions.question_text: Looking at the overhead gantry signals in the image, what do these permanent control signs mean?

options.a: I must switch immediately from lane 2 to lane 1.
options.b: Lanes 1 and 2 are for fast traffic, while lanes 3 and 4 are for slow traffic.
options.c: I may not use lanes 3 and 4.

questions.explanation: Overhead gantry signals directly control the availability of specific lanes, with a red 'X' expressly indicating that a lane is completely closed to traffic moving in your direction. Because lanes 3 and 4 currently display this red 'X', the rule dictates that you are strictly prohibited from driving in those lanes under any circumstances.

questions.question_text: In the image, you are driving. A police officer is standing in the junction. What is correct?

options.a: Wait at the crossroads until the officer waves.
options.b: Cross the crossroads at a brisk pace.
options.c: Stop immediately and wait for a different signal from the officer.

questions.explanation: When a police officer regulating traffic stands completely sideways to your line of approach, this physical stance acts as a green light for your direction. The rule dictates that you should not wait for further waves or signals, but rather cross the crossroads promptly at a brisk pace to keep the traffic flowing efficiently.
